clue.text: Little girl read out first of lessons at church

indicators.note: a word put out of order has its letters thrown about

parts.note: a short form of the girl's name Catherine
the four letters of this word, rearranged

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A young girl reads aloud the first lesson at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At church' looks like where the reading happens, but 'church' alone is the definition and 'at' only joins it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, holding the bishop's throne.

clue.text: The Stones' memorial?

parts.note: surface reading: the Rolling Stones rock band
setter's reading: a monument built from a heap of stones

explanation.walkthrough: The capital S and apostrophe point to the band, but the clue wants a memorial made of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a mound of rough stones piled up as a landmark or monument to the dead.

clue.text: May precede tavern in the town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first name that comes before the surname of the former UK prime minister May
second meaning: the words that come before this phrase in an old drinking song's title

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings use 'precede': the answer comes before May in a politician's name, and before 'tavern in the town' in the song 'There's a Tavern in the Town', read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May was a British prime minister, and 'There is a tavern in the town' is a well-known folk song.

clue.text: Set out, covering team departures

indicators.note: letters set out are laid out afresh in a different order
something covering another goes around it, so these letters wrap the other piece

parts.note: the three letters of this word, rearranged
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Players set out on the field, covering for team-mates who have left.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits are ways out or acts of leaving, so they are departures in the plural.

clue.text: Pull back leading troops president upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top
the leading part of a word is its front letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
Jimmy Carter, US president

explanation.surface: A president is upset as his leading troops are pulled back from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to draw something back in, as a cat retracts its claws.

clue.text: City's tired wingers' desire to get to final

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, with the possessive 'S

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the two end letters of the word
an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: A football side's weary wingers are still hungry to reach the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: The final is not a match here but the adjective, as in a last effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch attempt is a final desperate effort made when everything else has failed.

clue.text: Maximum resentment reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is heard rather than seen

parts.note: pique is a fit of wounded resentment

explanation.surface: A news story on the highest level of public resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the highest point or level reached, so it serves as a noun meaning the maximum.

clue.text: Hear cop busted illegal fisherman

indicators.note: something busted is broken, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: News that a policeman has arrested someone fishing without a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A poacher takes game or fish from land or water where he has no right to hunt.

clue.text: Section of grammar review of Aeneid (three chapters)

indicators.note: a review reworks material into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: Virgil's epic poem, taken letter for letter
C is the standard abbreviation for chapter, three times over

explanation.surface: A schoolroom critique of three chapters of Virgil's Aeneid, as Latin grammar homework.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets add the three Cs to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidence is the part of grammar dealing with inflections, the changing endings of words.

clue.text: Graves would be included here

parts.note: surface reading: burial places, as if in a cemetery register
setter's reading: Graves is a Bordeaux wine, so it appears on a restaurant's menu of drinks

explanation.walkthrough: Graves is a red or white wine from the Graves district of Bordeaux; the capital is hidden at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine list is the restaurant card naming the wines on offer, which might include a Graves.

clue.text: Meeting conducted with spirit?

parts.note: surface reading: a lively, energetic meeting
setter's reading: a gathering where a medium contacts the ghost of the dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'With spirit' sounds like enthusiasm; here the spirit is a ghost, and a medium conducts the session.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a gathering at which people try to communicate with the dead through a medium.

clue.text: Shows scorn but never without five on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a steamship, so the letters sit inside the abbreviation for one
without means lacking, so a piece is dropped from the word

parts.note: the word as written, in its short poetic form ne'er once a letter goes
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone shows contempt but never misses five people on the team sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: SS is a steamship, so being on board means inside S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneers are contemptuous smiles or remarks, so a person who sneers shows scorn.

clue.text: He worked with deadly chemical

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so the letters are remade together

parts.note: the letters as written
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A scientist handled a lethal substance in the lab.
explanation.definitionFit: An aldehyde is an organic compound, such as formaldehyde, containing a CHO group.

clue.text: Latest bulletin about coups d'etat Scot dismissed

indicators.note: about means turned around every which way, so the remaining letters are scrambled
dismissed means sent away, so those letters leave the phrase

parts.note: the letters as written
the letters as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: The newest news report on the overthrow of governments, with a Scottish minister sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is the most recent piece of news or information on a developing story.

clue.text: Trousers added to rowing team

parts.note: plus means with something added
a four is a racing boat with four oarsmen, here in the plural

explanation.surface: Trousers handed out as extra kit to the rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus fours are baggy knickerbockers gathered below the knee, traditionally worn by golfers.

clue.text: They may pass on what they know

definitions.text: They may pass on what they know

parts.note: surface reading: people who share their knowledge with others, like teachers
setter's reading: candidates who succeed in a test on the strength of what they have learned

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' reads as hand down, but it means get through a test on the basis of their knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Examinees are candidates sitting a test, who succeed if their knowledge is good enough.

clue.text: Codebreaker admitted to private education

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Alan Turing, who cracked German codes at Bletchley Park
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wartime codebreaker was given a place at a private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutoring is one-to-one teaching by a paid tutor, a private form of education.

clue.text: Protection for half a day is almost hell

indicators.note: half a word keeps only one of its two halves

parts.note: the day of the week, cut to its first half

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the contracted form, as in it's
Hades is the underworld of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Seeking shelter for part of a day in heat that is almost hellish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day' has to become a particular day, Sunday, before it can be halved.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is a parasol or awning that gives protection from the sun's glare.

clue.text: Caught nieces playing with physics, say

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone is caught playing physics games with their nieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics is one branch of science, so the 'say' marks it as an example of the category.

clue.text: Comes into force?

parts.note: surface reading: a law that takes effect
setter's reading: one who joins an armed force such as the army

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally describes a new law; here the force is a military one, which a recruit joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enlists signs up for military service, joining one of the armed forces.

clue.text: Nobbled one horse dealer

indicators.note: a nobbled racehorse has been tampered with, so the letters are interfered with

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A crooked horse dealer has doped one of the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse dealer' reads as one phrase, but 'horse' is fodder and 'dealer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosier deals in stockings, socks and knitted underwear, so he is a type of trader.

clue.text: Smear tactics from one leaving Orcadian, maybe

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: an Orcadian comes from Orkney, a group of islands off Scotland
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Political mudslinging drives a native of Orkney to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is false spoken defamation, the kind of attack used to smear someone's name.

clue.text: Lights out here in France, it's decreed

indicators.note: out means on the outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: lights are animal lungs, eaten as offal
the French word for here

explanation.surface: A French order that the lights go out here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights out' wants to be read together as switching off, but lights are the lungs of an animal sold by butchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something official has been authorised by those in power, as a decree is.

clue.text: Feature of Barnet Hospital rebuilt losing house

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form
losing means going without, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: the letters as written
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Barnet Hospital, a London hospital, is being rebuilt and has lost a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough, but it is rhyming slang: Barnet Fair means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaits are braided lengths of hair, a feature of a hairstyle, which the slang calls one's barnet.

clue.text: Up mountain, two sharp bends and a square

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
the letter Z has two sharp bends, as on a road sign warning of a double bend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain road with two hairpin bends leads up to a village square.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town, from the Spanish word.

clue.text: They could be spare in City restaurant

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Seats in a city-centre restaurant might be going spare.
explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is the extra wheel a car carries, and also slang for a roll of fat round the waist, apt in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyres are rubber wheel coverings, and a car carries a spare one for punctures.

clue.text: Fruit, almost a pound once topped

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is cut
topped means having its top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a quid is British slang for one pound sterling
the letters as written

explanation.surface: Fruit that once cost nearly a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped yellow fruit used for jelly and preserves.

clue.text: Accepted model flag for the regiment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the agreed benchmark others are measured against
second meaning: a military banner carried by a regiment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepted' and 'model' could each define the answer alone, making it a triple definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a recognised benchmark of quality and the banner or colours of a military unit.

clue.text: Could be Wight or Lewis, (Lewis) partially!

indicators.note: partially means only in part, so the letters come from parts of the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters straddle the repeated name

explanation.surface: A quiz question about British islands, with the name Lewis said twice, the second time half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Wight and Lewis are British islands; the repeated Lewis in brackets supplies the letters, end of one into start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Wight off southern England and Lewis in the Outer Hebrides are both islands, each formally named with this word.

clue.text: Second donkey wandering afar to small tree

indicators.note: wandering means straying from a set path, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an ass is a donkey
the four letters of this word, rearranged
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A second donkey wanders far off towards a little tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassafras is a North American tree of the laurel family, with aromatic bark.
